task: Write one sentence of your own using the word abject. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know abject should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Sailors rescued from the drifting lifeboat were in an abject state: sunburned, silent, and too weak to climb the ladder unaided.
Shabby is far milder than abject — a shabby coat is merely worn and frayed, and nothing about it suggests real misery.
Wretched is weaker than abject — wretched names deep misery, while abject strips away the last of a person's comfort and dignity as well.

Squalid describes filthy, degraded surroundings — a squalid room, a squalid alley. Abject covers a person's whole condition: misery so complete that dignity is gone. A place is squalid; a person, an apology, or a failure is abject.

Destitute means utterly without money or the basic necessities of life, and it measures what a person materially lacks. Abject measures how completely misery has crushed someone — an abject figure may still have shelter yet has lost all dignity. Destitute counts possessions; abject weighs the whole condition.
